scope: Owned experimental hostap 2.12 build enables 500 ms bounded MKA transmission while retaining normal Hello 2000 ms and lifetime 6000 ms constants. The timer preserves subsecond units.

A bounded one-second PN sample history replaces the old get_lpn method that explicitly assumed a two-second transmit interval. The advertised lower bound uses next PN so idle transmission does not preserve an old frame indefinitely.

The history and finite delayed-frame tests are experimental implementation work. Full IEEE 802.1X normative conformance and every key rollover/control-delay case remain separate. The original hostap receive-delay code already programs Linux receive lowest PN.
